ARMY RULE / DOSAGES



Combat Drugs
Combat Elixirs
Combat Drugs includes dosages, Pain Brings Clarity and Stupefied. There are eight core
Warband Elixirs; selected detachments can add further Warband choices. A Signature Elixir
is accessible only where its datasheet or another ability grants access. A rule permitting one
Combat Elixir from this codex can select Warband, Signature, detachment or enhancement
elixirs, but cannot refresh an expended once-per-battle use.
Taking a dose
At the start of a phase allowed by an accessible elixir, an eligible unit can activate it and
take a Leadership test. Resolve the elixir whether the test passes or fails. On a failure, the
unit suffers 2 mortal wounds, then becomes Battle-shocked, in that order. Wounds lost to
the dosage do not themselves trigger Pain Brings Clarity.
Multiple doses
A unit can activate several different accessible elixirs while eligible, taking a separate test
for each. It cannot activate the same elixir again while that elixir is active; identical effects
do not stack. Battle-shock prevents new ordinary doses but does not end existing effects.
Daemons and bound bodies
Daemons do not take ordinary doses or become Stupefied unless specifically permitted.
Bound Excess grants persistent normal benefits directly to its model. Daemon abilities can
administer elixirs to eligible recipients without the Daemon consuming them. Fulgrim has
his own exception.
Scope of benefits
An ordinary dose affects the whole receiving unit, including attached models, except where
its text names a particular model or weapon. Elixirs can modify only attacks or rolls that
actually occur: Torrent has no Hit roll, and Advance-and-shoot permission does not remove
unrelated restrictions.
Timing outside the normal phase
An ability that grants an out-of-phase activation must say so. Becoming Stupefied ignores
the selected elixir's activation window and extends it until recovery. Benefits still apply only
to their specified actions: Hallucinogens prevents Movement-phase Overwatch; it does not
create Charge-phase Overwatch.
raw_pages.6:
ARMY RULE / CLARITY AND EXCESS



Pain and Stupefied
Pain Brings Clarity
A unit with Combat Drugs that is Battle-shocked but not Stupefied immediately ceases to be
Battle-shocked when either of the following occurs:
1. A friendly Emperor's Children unit or an enemy unit within 6" of it is destroyed.
2. An enemy unit within 6" of it fails a Battle-shock test.
For a unit being destroyed, measure the distance immediately before its last model is
removed. Losing wounds or individual models does not trigger this rule. The receiving unit
does not need to have caused the destruction. Its attacks destroying an enemy unit farther
than 6" away do not ordinarily trigger this rule. Explicit abilities can grant additional ways to
invoke it.
Become Stupefied
At the end of your Command phase, after earlier scoring, an eligible unit can become
Stupefied. Choose one accessible Combat Elixir, ignoring its activation timing. It becomes
Battle-shocked, ends all other elixir effects, and gains the chosen elixir's normal effect and
its amplified Stupefied effect. No dosage test is taken for this choice.
While Stupefied
The selected elixir lasts until recovery, overriding its normal duration. The unit cannot take
new doses or ordinarily change its selected elixir. It automatically fails Leadership and
Battle-shock tests and cannot cease to be Battle-shocked, including through Pain Brings
Clarity. An explicit exception can override this.
Recovery
In your next Command phase, at the normal Battle-shock step, automatically pass this
unit's recovery test. Resolve this even if it would not otherwise need a test. This explicitly
overrides automatic failure: Stupefied and its selected elixir end, and Battle-shock clears.
The unit may become Stupefied again at the end of that phase.
Exceptions
Fulgrim is not Battle-shocked while Stupefied. Lucius can suspend the state. The Threnody
does not recover normally and has an objective-based lucidity ability. Bound Excess
ordinarily prohibits Stupefied. These exceptions are described on their sheets.
raw_pages.7:
SEPARATE ARMY RULE / BOUND DAEMONS



Bound Excess
Bound Excess
When mustering your army, select two different Warband Elixirs for this model. Their
normal effects are always active for this model, ignoring activation timing and duration. It
cannot activate additional Combat Elixirs or become Stupefied. If an effect requires an
enemy selection, make that selection at the start of each applicable phase. Ordinary
Battle-shock still applies.
Separate army rule
Only units listing Bound Excess in their Army rules field have this rule. It is separate from
Combat Drugs, Sublime Strategist and Manifestation. Ordinary recipients have two
permanent normal effects, no personal dosages and no Stupefied. Fulgrim does not have
Bound Excess; Master of Excess is his own datasheet ability.
Recipients: foot Daemon Prince, winged Daemon Prince, Julius Kaesoron, Doomrider, Idol
of Sublime Perfection, Defiler, Maulerfiend, Heldrake and Cacophant.
Fulgrim: Master of Excess
Fulgrim does not have this army rule. His separate Master of Excess datasheet ability grants
his two permanent Warband Elixir selections and retains and amplifies both when he
becomes Stupefied, alongside a third accessible elixir. Use his datasheet for Master of
Excess and Sovereign of Sensation.
Exultation in Ruin
After this unit has shot or fought, if its attacks destroyed one or more enemy units, select
one friendly non-Daemon EC unit within 6". That unit resolves Pain Brings Clarity as though
an enemy unit had been destroyed within 6" of it. This cannot clear Battle-shock while
Stupefied.
Recipients: Defiler, Maulerfiend, Heldrake and Cacophant. Giving a Prince Bound Excess
does not also give it Exultation in Ruin.
Personal permanent benefits
Permanent selected effects apply to the model that has Bound Excess. They are not doses
administered to its unit. Separately, Fulgrim's Master of Excess benefits are personal: his
Phoenix Guard do not inherit the selections, and Stupefied affecting the Attached unit does
not erase his explicit retained benefits.
Not bound engines
The Agoniser and Threnody are interred mortal warriors, not Daemon models. They use
Combat Drugs and their own datasheet exceptions. The Stage is non-Daemon Mounted, not
a Vehicle. Chaos Spawn and Greater Chaos Spawn are non-Daemon Beasts in this roster.
Effects requiring selection
A permanent Soporific Musk effect uses its normal defensive benefit. Its amplified enemy
selection is unavailable to ordinary Bound Excess models, because they cannot become
Stupefied. Fulgrim makes any amplified target selection at the start of the applicable Fight
phase, or immediately if the effect is gained during that phase.
raw_pages.8:
SEPARATE ARMY RULE / COMMAND POINTS



Sublime Strategist
Sublime Strategist
At the start of the battle round, if a model with this army rule is your Warlord, gain 1CP.
This army rule is separate from Combat Drugs. Only models whose datasheets list Sublime
Strategist have it. It awards one CP at the start of each battle round if your Warlord
qualifies; other eligible commanders do not each generate another CP.

Excluded models

Interaction with drugs
Ordinary Battle-shock or Stupefied does not turn off Sublime Strategist: its text does not

raw_pages.9:
EIGHT UNIVERSAL COMBAT ELIXIRS



Warband Elixirs
Hyperstimulants
Activate: start of your Movement phase. Duration: end of the turn.
Ranged attacks made by this unit have Assault, and making an Advance move does not
prevent this unit from declaring a charge that turn. If Stupefied, also add 2 to Advance
rolls made for this unit.
Frenzon
Activate: start of your Movement phase. Duration: end of the turn.
Making a Fall Back move does not prevent this unit from shooting or declaring a charge that
turn. If Stupefied, also add 3" to the distance models in this unit can move when making a
Fall Back move.
Adrenal Surge
Activate: start of either Fight phase. Duration: end of the phase.
Add 2 to the Strength characteristic of melee weapons equipped by models in this unit. If
Stupefied, Each time a model in this unit makes a Pile-in or Consolidation move, it can
move up to 6". It does not need to end that move closer to the closest enemy model,
provided it ends as close as possible to the closest enemy unit. Other requirements of that
move still apply.
Razor's Edge

Improve the Armour Penetration characteristic of this unit's attacks by 1. If Stupefied,
those attacks also have [LETHAL HITS].
raw_pages.10:
EIGHT UNIVERSAL COMBAT ELIXIRS



Warband Elixirs / II
Soporific Musk

Subtract 1 from Hit rolls for melee attacks that target this unit. If Stupefied, select one
enemy unit within Engagement Range of this unit. That enemy unit loses Fights First until
the end of the phase.
Hallucinogens

Models in this unit have Feel No Pain 5+. If Stupefied, each time a model in this unit is

after this unit has fought, or at the end of the phase, whichever happens first.
raw_pages.11:
GENERAL RULES



Psychic and weapon reference
Psyker levels
A Psyker can use abilities with a total level no greater than its Psyker Level each battle
round. A power can be used no more than once per phase. Each listed power requires its
caster's unit not to be Battle-shocked. Roll one D6: on 1 the unit becomes Battle-shocked,
but resolve the power. This roll is not a Leadership or Battle-shock test. Psychic weapon
attacks do not consume this budget unless specified.
 Psyker                                 Level   Role

 Raptureweaver                          1       Defensive ward and reactive movement

 Torment Oracle                         2       Battle-shock and forced movement

 Sibyl of Excess                        3       Mortal protection and relocation

 Shalaxi Helbane                        2       Hunting and terror

 Syll'Esske                             2       Melee support and Manifestation

 Keeper of Secrets                      3       Greater daemon support

 Tranceweaver                           1       Daemonette support

 Contorted Epitome                      3       Protection, terror and relocation

 Choir of Unmaking                      1       Psychic infantry; level per unit

Current weapon conventions
Flamers use fixed attacks with Blast. Sonic blasters and screamer pistols are Strength 6.
The sonic combi-weapon profile remains Strength 5. All sonic ranged weapons have at least
Blast 1; blastmasters have Blast 2. A specifically printed higher Blast value takes
precedence. D6+1 Damage is replaced by D3+3; this is not a blanket replacement of all D6
rolls.
Blast X and Cleave X
When all attacks with the weapon target one enemy unit, add X attack dice for each full five
models in that target, using the core rule's counting step. Blast applies to ranged weapons;
Cleave to melee weapons. Cleave does not spill damage between models.
Hunter profiles
A profile labelled Hunter: Monster/Vehicle can target only Monster or Vehicle units. Its
profile is an alternative, not an additional weapon.
Close-Quarters and Torrent
Use Close-Quarters under the eleventh-edition shooting rules. Torrent automatically hits.
Blast weapons remain subject to engagement restrictions unless an ability explicitly
removes Blast or otherwise permits the attack. Eidolon's amplified Death Scream is one
such exception.
Restoring wounds to a unit
Heal a wounded model first. Excess restored wounds can return destroyed non-Character
models and continue healing them, up to Starting Strength. Do not return a destroyed
Character or an entirely destroyed unit unless an ability explicitly permits it. A single-model
unit cannot exceed its starting wounds.
raw_pages.12:
GENERAL RULES / CURRENT TERMINOLOGY



Eleventh-edition move reference
Disembark moves
A disembarking unit is set up wholly within 3" of its Transport, following the core placement
restrictions. A shock disembark move permits disembarking after that Transport Advances,
but the passengers cannot declare a charge that turn. An assault disembark move permits
the passengers to charge after their Transport makes a Normal move. Use the granting
ability and all other core restrictions.
Ingress moves
Ingress is the core move used to arrive from Reserves, including when using Deep Strike.
Apply each unit's printed arrival distance. A rule that repositions a unit or summons a
Legions of Excess unit does not become an ingress rule merely because it sets models up
on the battlefield.
Normal shooting
An out-of-phase rule specifying normal shooting uses the normal shooting procedure. It
does not become Snap Shooting merely because it occurs outside your Shooting phase. Its
printed target restrictions and other core restrictions still apply.
Damaged X
While a model with Damaged X has X or fewer wounds remaining, subtract 1 from its Hit
rolls. Fulgrim instead retains The Phoenician Prince, with its own threshold and modifiers.
Explosives and Close-Quarters
Explosives is the current keyword used in place of Grenades on the affected datasheets.
Close-Quarters is a weapon ability; a weapon named a pistol still uses its printed profile and
abilities.
Conditional attack abilities
A qualifier such as Lethal Hits: non-MONSTER/VEHICLE applies only when targeting units
without either excluded keyword. An unqualified Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits ability retains
its normal scope.
raw_pages.13:
ALLIED FACTION / ACCESS



Legions of Excess
Separate faction
Legions of Excess are allies, not Emperor's Children units. Choose Emperor's Children as
your Army Faction. Your Warlord must be an eligible Emperor's Children model. Legions of
Excess cannot be chosen as the Army Faction through this codex.
Exclusive detachment access
Only Carnival of Excess (3DP), Perfumed Procession (1DP) and Ritual Host (1DP) permit
Legions of Excess allies. Carnival permits 500/1,000/1,500 allied points at Incursion/Strike
Force/Onslaught. Perfumed Procession and Ritual Host each permit 500 points; their
allowances stack to 1,000 when both are selected. Allies count toward normal army points
and copy limits.
Bound EC daemons remain EC
Fulgrim, Julius Kaesoron, Doomrider, the two Daemon Princes, the Idol and daemon engines
remain Emperor's Children units. They do not require one of the three allied-access
detachments and do not gain Manifestation. Their own listed army rules apply.
No personal drugs
Legions of Excess units use Manifestation, not Combat Drugs or Bound Excess. Their
Daemon keyword can make them eligible for a greater daemon aura regardless of army
allegiance. A rule naming Emperor's Children does not automatically affect allied units.
Summoning pool
When mustering, pay for the allied units and declare any legal attachments. These units
begin in a summoning pool off the battlefield and enter through the rituals in this chapter.
The pool is used for these rituals, not as an ordinary Deep Strike deployment or Strategic
Reserves move.
Detachment benefits
Use the full detachment entries for Living Elixir auras, expanded mortal ritual access,
Daemonic Empowerment and Mortal Anchors. Their benefits do not change a unit's faction.
raw_pages.14:
SEPARATE ARMY RULE / LEGIONS OF EXCESS



Manifestation
Arrival and maximum
Each time a unit with this army rule is summoned, it gains D3 Manifestation points. Lesser
daemons have a maximum of 3; Greater Daemons have a maximum of 6. A larger
maximum does not change the initial D3 roll.
Feed on excess
While this unit is on the battlefield, each time A UNIT within 6" of it is destroyed, or A UNIT
within 6" of it fails a Battle-shock test, it gains 1 Manifestation point. Friendly and enemy
units qualify, whether Daemons or non-Daemons. Measure a destroyed unit's range
immediately before its last model is removed.
Gain cap
A unit can gain at most 1 Manifestation point per phase, including points granted by psychic
powers and other abilities, and cannot exceed its maximum. Gains can occur in either
player's turn. Already being Battle-shocked grants nothing; an actual failed test is required.
A required test automatically failed by a Stupefied unit can trigger this rule.
Instability
At the end of each phase IN YOUR TURN, after resolving Manifestation gains for that phase,
each unit with this army rule loses 1 point. If it has 0 points, it immediately becomes
Debound. There is no ordinary point loss in your opponent's turn. Furies lose points only at
the end of YOUR Fight phase.
Debound
Remove the unit from the battlefield and return it to your summoning pool, retaining its
surviving models and their remaining wounds. It can subsequently be summoned again.
Becoming Debound is not being destroyed, but does trigger rules for leaving the battlefield.
Resummoning does not restore models or wounds; roll initial Manifestation again. Persistent
effects such as the Furies' collected OC remain in effect.
End-of-phase abilities
A unit already removed as Debound cannot make a subsequent battlefield move. Resolve
normal sequencing for simultaneous end-of-phase abilities; The Final Bow explicitly resolves
before the Masque is removed.
raw_pages.15:
RITUAL / LEVEL 1 PSYCHIC POWER



Lesser daemon summoning
Lesser Daemonic Ritual (Psychic Level 1)
At the start of a phase in your turn, one friendly non-Daemon Psyker whose unit is not
Battle-shocked can use this power. Roll one D6 as a psychic roll. On a 1, its unit becomes
Battle-shocked. Regardless of the result, resolve the following effect. Select one Legions of
Excess unit in your summoning pool, excluding Greater Daemons. Set it up wholly within 6"
of that Psyker and more than 8" horizontally from all enemy models. It gains D3
Manifestation points. No sacrifice is required.
Ritual limit and timing
Each Psyker can perform one summoning ritual per turn. The lesser ritual uses 1 level of its
normal psychic budget and follows this codex's psychic procedure. It does not bypass
Battle-shock. A summoned unit loses a point at the end of its arrival phase normally. A
summoned unit can declare a charge in your Charge phase if otherwise eligible, including
when summoned at its start; summoning does not itself prohibit this.
Furies exception
A friendly Daemon Psyker can also perform the lesser ritual, but can select only Furies of
Slaanesh. This exception does not allow a Daemon Psyker to summon other lesser units or
Greater Daemons.
Attached units
Declare attachments when mustering. An eligible Leader and Bodyguard are summoned
together as one Attached unit, using one ritual and one shared Manifestation roll and total
while attached. The whole Attached unit must fit the setup restrictions and becomes
Debound together. Retain its surviving models, wounds and attachment when it returns to
the pool. Destroyed Leaders do not return unless an explicit ability permits it.
Lesser Epic Heroes
The Masque and Syll'Esske use the lesser ritual and maximum of 3. Being an Epic Hero or
Monster does not itself make a unit a Greater Daemon.
raw_pages.16:
RITUAL / SACRIFICE REQUIRED



Greater daemon summoning
Greater Daemonic Ritual
At the start of your Charge phase, select one friendly non-Daemon Psyker that has not
performed a summoning ritual this turn. Select one OTHER friendly non-Daemon Infantry
unit within 6" of that Psyker to sacrifice. Destroy the sacrificed unit. Then select one Greater
Daemon from your summoning pool and set it up wholly within 6" of the Psyker and more
than 8" horizontally from all enemy models. It gains D3 Manifestation points and can
declare a charge that phase.
Cost and sequence
The ritual consumes that Psyker's summoning ritual for the turn and requires the sacrificed
unit. It is not an additional levelled psychic power. Resolve the sacrifice and its destruction
triggers before setting up the daemon. The arriving daemon cannot gain a point from its
own sacrifice because it was not on the battlefield when that unit was destroyed. Daemons
already nearby can gain normally.
Greater Daemons
Shalaxi Helbane and Keepers of Secrets use this ritual and have a Manifestation maximum
of 6. Each resummoning requires another ritual and sacrifice. Do not restore lost models or
wounds through resummoning.
 Initial D3             Without additional gains or an exception

 1                      Debounds at the end of your Charge phase.

 2                      Can fight, then Debounds at the end of your Fight phase.

 3                      Survives your Fight phase with 1 point remaining.

Existing army interactions
The sacrifice is a real destruction and can trigger other rules normally. Debinding is only
leaving the battlefield; it is not a sacrifice or destruction.
raw_pages.17:
REALITY DISTORTION / ALL ALLEGIANCES



Greater daemon auras
Reality Unravels - 12 inch Aura
While a unit is within 12" of one or more Greater Daemons with this ability, if it is a Daemon
unit, improve the AP of its melee weapons by 1; otherwise, worsen its Leadership
characteristic by 1. This affects friendly and enemy units alike. Multiple instances of Reality
Unravels do not stack.
Worsening Leadership means making its characteristic less favourable under the core rules.
This is the oppressive effect on non-Daemons; it does not improve their chance of passing.
The AP benefit also applies to enemy Daemons and to EC Daemon models such as the Idol,
Princes and Fulgrim.
Keeper: Palace of Sensation - 6 inch Aura
At the start of either Fight phase, every non-Daemon unit within 6" of the Keeper must take
a Battle-shock test. Friendly and enemy units are affected. Each Keeper resolves its own
aura.
Shalaxi: The Hunting Ground - 6 inch Aura
Whenever any other unit within 6" of Shalaxi is selected to Fall Back, it must first take a
Battle-shock test. If failed, it cannot Fall Back that phase. Friendly and enemy units,
including Daemons, are affected.
Interaction with Manifestation
Actual failed tests and units destroyed can feed nearby Manifestation normally. Apply the
1-point-per-phase gain cap. Do not grant points merely because a unit remains
Battle-shocked. Reality Unravels never grants Combat Drugs or Bound Excess.
Distinct personal abilities
The auras do not replace Shalaxi's quarry, The Hunt Sustains or psychic powers. Reality
Unravels replaces the Keeper's former friendly-only melee AP aura; those two AP auras are
not both present.

Once per turn, during the Shooting or Fight phase, when Lucius is destroyed by an attack
made by an enemy unit, the controller of that attacking unit must select one non-Epic

the attacking unit contains no eligible host, no marker is placed. Remove the marker before
destroying a successfully possessed host so its destruction does not cancel that successful
return.

the current turn and immediately cease to be Battle-shocked. This explicitly overrides the
normal restriction.

penalties are suspended, and it can take new doses normally. At the end of that turn, it
becomes Stupefied and Battle-shocked again; other elixirs end and the original selected
elixir's Stupefied effect resumes. This does not spend a new activation, refresh a
once-per-battle use or extend the original next Command-phase recovery.

OPTIONAL FORMAT / NEW PLAYTEST MATERIAL



Combat Patrol
The Exultant Procession
Fixed force: one Lord Exultant with bolt pistol, plasma pistol, Phoenix power spear and close
combat weapon; five Tormentors including an Obsessionist; five Infractors including an
Obsessionist; six Noise Marines with four sonic blasters and two blastmasters. The Lord joins
the Infractors. Use the datasheets in this book.
Patrol army rules
Use Combat Drugs, Pain Brings Clarity, Stupefied and Sublime Strategist. Different elixirs
can be stacked using the normal dosage procedure; no additional one-dose limit applies.
The Icons of Excess retain their printed ability.
Patrol construction
Use no detachments, enhancements or additional units. This fixed force is 450 points at this
book's roster costs. This is a custom Patrol, not an official balanced replacement; agree its
use with your opponent.
Patrol stratagem: Measured Dose / 1CP
WHEN: Start of a phase in which a friendly unit can legally take a dose. TARGET: That
eligible unit. EFFECT: Activate one accessible elixir without its dosage Leadership test. Its
normal duration applies.
Patrol stratagem: Refuse the Silence / 1CP
WHEN: Your Command phase, immediately before a friendly Patrol unit takes a Battle-shock
test. TARGET: That unit. EFFECT: It automatically passes that test.
Patrol objective: A Perfect Performance
Once per battle round, at the end of your turn, score 2VP if one or more enemy units were
destroyed by attacks made by your Stupefied units that turn. Maximum 10VP. Use this only
if both players agree to a format that includes faction secondary objectives.
Use the agreed Combat Patrol mission, terrain and primary scoring. These optional rules do
not change the main codex datasheets or normal game construction.
raw_pages.126:
OPTIONAL CRUSADE MODULE / NEW PLAYTEST MATERIAL



Campaign: The Pursuit of Excess
Use this short module alongside your chosen Crusade campaign rules. It does not replace
that campaign's supply limit, experience, Battle Honours, scars, requisitions or mission
sequence.
Research ledger
After each battle, gain 1 Research mark if a non-Daemon unit took three different elixirs
during that battle, and 1 if a Stupefied unit destroyed an enemy unit. Gain at most 2 marks
per battle. Record which condition was met; repeated qualifying units do not grant
additional marks.
Requisition: Refine the Formula / 1RP
After a battle, spend 3 Research marks and 1 Requisition point. Select one non-Epic Hero,
non-Daemon unit with Combat Drugs on your Order of Battle. It gains the Formula
Familiarity Battle Honour below. Count this against its Battle Honour limit.
Formula Familiarity
Select one Warband Elixir and record it. Once per battle, when this unit takes an ordinary
dose of that elixir, re-roll its dosage Leadership test. This does not prevent the
consequences of a failed re-roll or permit a dose while ineligible.
Agenda: Catalogue the Sensation
Select one eligible non-Epic Hero unit before the battle. It gains 1XP if it invokes Pain Brings
Clarity at least once, and 1XP if it destroys an enemy unit while Stupefied. Maximum 2XP.
Choose this in place of one normal Agenda, not in addition to your allowance.
Battle scar: Sensory Exhaustion
If your campaign calls for a new scar and permits a faction scar, you can choose this instead
of rolling: subtract 1 from this unit's dosage Leadership tests. Remove it using your
campaign's normal scar-removal procedure.
Campaign rewards do not enter ordinary matched-play lists. Permanent Warband selections
from Bound Excess are not ordinary dosages and cannot earn the three-elixir research
condition.
raw_pages.127:
EDITORIAL RECORD / IRONBUILT AUDIT



Edition 3.1 wording update
Wording sources
Compared the Emperor's Children 10e and transition entries with the current Adeptus
Astartes (Codex) entries in IRONBUILT. This pass updates core terminology and resolution
timing; it retains the project's custom roster, profiles, prices, distances and elixir effects.
Transport moves
The Rhino now names a shock disembark move after Advancing. The Land Raider uses an
assault disembark move after a Normal move. Violent Disembarkation targets the
embarked passengers when they are selected to disembark and permits an assault
disembark move. Capacity and passenger restrictions are unchanged.
Shooting and fighting
Return-fire abilities specify normal shooting. Fight-on-death effects use the current
sequence: retain a qualifying destroyed model until its unit has fought or the phase ends.
Euphoric Numbness remains a 4+ roll for each eligible model; Ecstatic Death remains 2+.
Psychic powers
Power headings use Psychic Level X, and each power prints the psychic-roll procedure. The
budget remains per battle round. Psychic weapon profiles do not acquire a power level.
Common rules
Damaged X appears in the Core field. Explosives replaces the older Grenades keyword.
Close-Quarters, ingress moves, secured objectives, wound healing and conditional attack
keywords use current terminology.
CP and Battle-shock
Sublime Strategist retains its Warlord-based battle-round CP gain. Discounts remain
discounts. Stratagems follow normal Battle-shock targeting restrictions; no new bypass or
repeated-use permission is added.
Bespoke mechanics
Combat Drugs, Stupefied, Pain Brings Clarity, Bound Excess and Manifestation retain their
custom scope and exceptions. Ritual summoning remains distinct from an ordinary ingress
move.
raw_pages.128:
EDITORIAL RECORD / ACCEPTED UPDATES



Edition 3.0 changes
Fifteen complete detachments
Ten 1DP, three 2DP and two 3DP packages replace the former placeholder chapter. Every
package has its detachment rule, enhancement or upgrade costs, and complete stratagem
entries. Coterie of the Conceited retains its published rules.
Allied access
Only Carnival of Excess (3DP), Perfumed Procession (1DP) and Ritual Host (1DP) permit
Legions of Excess allies. Carnival permits 500/1,000/1,500 allied points at Incursion/Strike
Force/Onslaught. Perfumed Procession and Ritual Host each permit 500 points; their
allowances stack to 1,000 when both are selected. Allies count toward normal army points
and copy limits.
Final detachment revisions
Kakophonic Conclave grants +1 ranged AP and Damage within 12 inches. Exquisite
Swordsmanship is selected individually when a unit that charged is selected to fight.
Executioner grants +1 melee Damage. Cut Down the Weak costs 2CP and triggers after an
enemy Falls Back in its Movement phase.
Movement and healing
Custom 3-inch Normal and reactive moves are now 6 inches. Chronostim retains the explicit
6-inch normal / 9-inch Stupefied exception. Revel in the Wreckage restores D3+3 wounds.
Quicksilver Mantle costs 15 points and grants +2 inches Move.
Elite technique
The Gilded Retinue uses Peerless Technique: select improved melee AP or worsened
incoming melee AP for each eligible unit at the start of each Fight phase.
Transports
Rhino capacity now admits Flawless Blades at two spaces each. Land Raider and Dreadclaw
include Colossi at three spaces each. Their revised disembark and arrival rules use the
eleventh-edition move terminology.
raw_pages.129:
EDITORIAL RECORD / EARLIER DECISIONS



Retained rules record
Fulgrim
485 points; T12, W18; strike D3+3 and Sustained Hits 2; sweep Cleave 2 and Sustained Hits
2. Tail poison requires actual damage and applies only -1 weapon Damage, minimum 1.
Fulgrim does not have Bound Excess; his permanent elixirs come from Master of Excess.
Combat Drugs
Dosage failure causes 2MW, then Battle-shock. Pain uses destruction and failed-test
triggers, not wound loss. Heightened Senses amplified effect re-rolls Hit rolls of 1. Multiple
different elixirs can stack while eligible.
Fulgrim doses
While not Stupefied, Fulgrim can take additional ordinary doses beyond his two permanent
selections, using normal timing and tests. While Stupefied, he retains and amplifies both
plus a third accessible elixir but cannot take new doses.
Bound daemons and commander CP
The Idol is an EC Daemon with Bound Excess and dispenses Nectar to mortal recipients.
Sublime Strategist remains a separate army rule on the ten listed command models; Lucius
and Doomrider do not receive it.
Legions of Excess
Thirteen allied datasheets retain Manifestation, summoning, greater daemon auras and
revised points. Loss occurs at each own phase end, except Furies. Debinding is leaving the
battlefield, not destruction.
Stratagem consistency
Stratagem entries use core targeting rules. The obsolete Heroic Intervention permission
while Battle-shocked has been removed from Aureate Vitae; its amplified Fights First benefit
remains.
Roster preservation
All 58 current datasheets remain. Retired units are not restored. Optional Combat Patrol
and campaign material remains separate from matched-play detachment selection.

raw_pages.135:
3DP / DETACHMENT RULE




The Grand Symphony
The Emperor's Children make war as a performance, amassing Stage Tokens through sonic violence before
spending them on escalating rewards.



  3 DP / THE GRAND SYMPHONY
  One 3DP selection. No other detachment can be selected at Strike Force.


Instruments of Excess

SONIC is an equipment-derived UNIT keyword. A friendly Emperor's Children unit containing at least
one model equipped with a weapon from the Sonic Weapons register (page 136) gains SONIC. If no
such model remains, it loses SONIC. SONIC is not a weapon keyword, and weapons not listed do not
become Sonic Weapons merely because their unit has SONIC.

Attached units count the equipment of their combined models. Determine eligibility from equipment
actually taken when mustering, not from every option printed on a datasheet. This keyword rule
applies throughout this codex; the Grand Symphony is the detachment that spends Stage Tokens.

Stage Tokens - building the performance

Starting pool: 0 Stage Tokens. Unspent tokens carry between rounds. Your pool cannot exceed 12
Stage Tokens; you can gain at most 6 in each battle round. Tokens are not CP, do not interact with
Stratagem cost rules, and are not gained by Legions of Excess units.

Damage verse: After a friendly EC unit finishes shooting in your Shooting phase, if one or more attacks
made by that unit with a listed Sonic Weapon caused an enemy model to lose one or more wounds,
gain 1 Stage Token. A unit can generate this reward only once per Shooting phase, no matter how
many weapons hit or how much damage it dealt.

Slaughter verse: Once per Shooting phase, after a friendly EC SONIC unit destroys an enemy unit with
a ranged attack made with a listed Sonic Weapon, gain 1 additional Stage Token. Resolve these token
gains before checking whether you can pay for Daemonic Encore.

Trigger precision: A successful Wound roll that is saved does not count as damage. Any enemy unit
destroyed by an attack from a friendly SONIC unit can trigger Daemonic Encore, but only a listed Sonic
Weapon generates the extra Slaughter verse token.

Available performances

Spend your stored Stage Tokens on the performances on page 137 at their specified timing. You must
have enough tokens before paying. The same Stage Tokens cannot fund more than one performance.
+1 Damage bonuses from Shattering Crescendo and The Grand Finale do not stack on the same
attack.

  Blastmasters                         Blastmaster; dreadblastmaster


  Large blastmasters                   Grand blastmaster; cathedral blastmaster


  Defiler armory                       Defiler blastmaster; sonic balespewer


  Heavy sonic                          Sonic destructor; cathedral sonic immolator


  Resonance                            Resonance cannon


  Specialist weapons                   Shriek cannon; grand vox array


  Named weapons                        Death Scream; The Eighth's Refrain


For a weapon printed with multiple named firing profiles (for example, crescendo and rupture, or a focused
profile), each printed profile of that listed weapon counts. Weapon variants with the same listed base name
count. A generic weapon with the words "sonic" only in an ability description does not qualify unless listed here.

Practical equipment examples

Always SONIC with printed standard equipment: Noise Marines, Lord Kakophonist, Eidolon, Ramos, Dissonant
Colossi, Threnody Dreadnought and Stage of Excess.

SONIC when the listed option is taken: Cacophant (resonance cannon), Defiler (Defiler blastmaster or sonic
balespewer), Palatine Ravager (sonic destructor or sonic blasters), Chaos Land Raider (cathedral blastmasters
or twin sonic blaster), Chaos Rhino (sonic combi-weapon), Heldrake (sonic balespewer), Excruciator Terminators
(sonic combi-weapon or shriek cannon), and any other EC unit with an equipped weapon from the register.

Not Sonic Weapons in this edition: Ghost whisper carbines and the doomfire projector. These profiles can be
reconsidered separately; they do not qualify simply for thematic similarity.

What SONIC does, and does not, mean

Stage Token generation requires attacks made with listed Sonic Weapons, not attacks with any gun in a SONIC
unit. By contrast, Shattering Crescendo can enhance a selected EC unit's ranged attacks, and The Grand Finale
can enhance all ranged weapons carried by SONIC units as specifically printed on page 137.

3DP / PERFORMANCE COSTS




Spend Stage Tokens
Choose between disrupting enemy formations, intensifying gunfire or materialising daemons at the climax of a
slaughter.


Discordant Overture - 2 Stage Tokens

WHEN: Your Shooting phase, after a friendly SONIC unit has shot and hit an enemy unit with a listed Sonic
Weapon. EFFECT: That enemy unit takes a Battle-shock test, subtracting 1 from the result. Resolve after that
attacking unit's shooting. Multiple Overtures cannot target the same unit in one phase.

Shattering Crescendo - 4 Stage Tokens

WHEN: Your Shooting phase, when you select one friendly EC unit to shoot. REQUIREMENT: Select one enemy
unit that was already hit by a listed Sonic Weapon earlier in the phase. EFFECT: Until the end of this phase, add
1 to the Damage characteristic of ranged attacks made by the selected EC unit that target that enemy unit.
Once per Shooting phase.

Daemonic Encore - 7 Stage Tokens

WHEN: Immediately after a friendly EC SONIC unit destroys an enemy unit with one or more of its ranged
attacks. Mark the position of the last model removed from that destroyed enemy unit. EFFECT: Create and
summon one unit of ten Daemonettes without paying any army points, without a summoner, without a sacrifice
and without a summoning-pool declaration.

Set up the first Daemonette model as close as possible to the last removed model's position; set up the
remaining models as close as possible while keeping the unit in coherency. Models cannot overlap occupied
bases or be placed in impassable positions. Ignore the ordinary 8-inch enemy-distance requirement: these
Daemonettes may be set up within Engagement Range of enemy units. This permission overrides only that
setup restriction.

The unit begins with 3 Manifestation points (maximum 3) and does not lose a point at the end of the phase in
which it appears. Afterwards it uses the ordinary Manifestation rules. If it becomes Debound, remove it from the
battle rather than return it to the summoning pool. It can fight and, if eligible, charge normally under core rules.
If all ten models cannot be placed legally in coherency, the summon cannot be performed and no tokens are
spent.

No per-turn or per-battle summoning cap. You can repeat Daemonic Encore every time you meet its trigger and
can pay the tokens. These free Daemonettes do not grant access to paid Legions of Excess allies or additional
free datasheets.

The Grand Finale - 9 Stage Tokens

WHEN: Start of your Shooting phase. EFFECT: Until the end of that phase, add 1 to the Damage characteristic of
ranged weapons equipped by models in friendly EC SONIC units when targeting enemy units within 12" of those
models. Once per battle. This bonus cannot stack with Shattering Crescendo on the same attack.

Version 3.2 - accepted changes

Kakophonic Conclave (2DP): Overwhelming Resonance now adds +1 Strength and improves AP by 1 for EC
ranged attacks against targets within 12"; its former unconditional +1 ranged Damage is removed. Its
enhancements and stratagems are otherwise unchanged.

New 3DP option: The Grand Symphony brings the total to 16 detachments (10 x 1DP; 3 x 2DP; 3 x 3DP). It adds
an equipment-derived SONIC unit keyword, Stage Tokens, four performances and unlimited token-paid free
Daemonette summons. No new datasheets are added.

Wargear points: Defiler Hades lascannon and heavy reaper autocannon each cost an additional 15 points per
equipped weapon. The points register and Defiler equipment page have been updated. This is the confirmed
GW-derived surcharge; no unverified costs were invented for custom resonance weapons.

Retained balance patch: All v3.1a unit-point reductions and the two Daemon Prince increases remain in force,
including the 250-point Chaos Land Raider, cheaper Spawn, and cheaper Legions of Excess daemons.

Placement exception: Daemonic Encore is intentionally allowed to place Daemonettes in Engagement Range
and has no per-game or per-turn quantity cap. Normal placement requirements still apply unless explicitly
overridden on page 137.
